Level 1

Platform map

Six pillars mirror the sidebar. Read the bullets here; open Go deeper only when you own that slice.

Build

Where people work

Inspector is the conversational workbench: question → semantic + memory context → agent loop → SQL/tools on Databricks → charts (Data Studio) → saved session.

  • Home dashboard — post-login health (estate, memory, logins).
  • Analytics dashboards — governed boards from pinned Inspector results.
  • Metrics — what KPIs mean; Teach — deliberate memory candidates.
  • Performance Lab — experiments; Bandits — which models/tools win; History — replay sessions.
Memory

What the system remembers

FOER injects attributed rules at chat time; overnight jobs synthesize new bullets from traces — no fine-tuning.

  • Daytime: retrieve → inject → run → attribute usefulness.
  • Overnight: reflect, label, curate, cluster (DAG).
  • Ops / Contributions — pipeline health and who taught what.
  • Marcus — post-turn reflection feeding memory and bandits.
Data estate

How data gets discoverable

Harvester jobs (T0–T3+) copy warehouse metadata into Aurora so Inspector harvested mode can search a catalog instead of raw SHOW TABLES.

  • Jobs — launch/monitor pipeline; Catalog — browse objects.
  • Mapper / Entities — business terms ↔ physical tables.
  • Lineage, Silo, Object detail — trust, orphans, per-table debug.
Govern

Who can do what

Entra SSO → JIT user in Aurora → roles + permissions on every API. Staging UI for Users, Policies, and Audit; Docs is the governed agent/tool catalog consumed at runtime.

  • Users — invite, role change, deactivate; needs user:* permissions.
  • Policies — policy_entry rules layered on roles.
  • Audit — writeAudit + staging lifecycle feed.
  • Docs catalog — publish agents/tools Inspector can attach.
Cross-cutting

Shared engines

Capabilities every surface depends on — not a separate “app” but plumbing behind Inspector and dashboards.

  • Semantic layer — models, metrics, promotion, NL intent.
  • Data Studio — profile SQL results → charts.
  • Auth — middleware + resolveAuth on APIs.
  • Harvester pipeline — ops view of T0–T3 factory.
Run & integrate

Deploy and external systems

Next.js on Beanstalk, harvest on Fargate, Aurora + Databricks + LLM providers. Inspector context mode chooses catalog vs warehouse discovery.

  • Deployment — ALB, health, ECS, schedules.
  • External APIs — env var names only in this guide.
  • DB dictionaries — memory tables vs full Prisma catalog.
Story

One Inspector question — end to end

The path that ties every pillar together. Follow left to right for a typical analytics question.

1AskUser chats in Inspector; picks harvested or warehouse_only.
2GroundSemantic context + FOER memory inject into the prompt.
3RunAgent loop, tools, SQL on Databricks; trajectory logged.
4ShowData Studio chart; optional pin to dashboard.

Tip

Two different “dashboards”

Same word in the product — different routes and purpose. Don’t mix them when explaining ALOFT.

Home dashboard

/dashboard — post-login health: estate, memory, logins, Inspector activity.

Analytics dashboards

/inspector/dashboards — governed, shareable boards from Inspector pins.

Summary

Big picture + connections

One paragraph, then how modules connect in the diagram below.

ALOFT D360 is a governed conversational analytics platform for warehouse data. People ask questions in Inspector; the platform grounds answers with harvested catalog + semantic definitions + FOER memory, executes read-only SQL on Databricks, renders charts, and saves work to dashboards and history. Overnight jobs and Marcus / bandits improve the next turn. Govern controls who can see and promote what.

How to use (in plain English)
1
Go to Build → Inspector. A new session starts automatically.
2
Choose Harvested (recommended) or Warehouse Only in the top bar.
3
Type your question in natural language. You can also attach specific tools or agents.
4
Watch the live stream: thinking, tool calls, and results appear as they happen.
5
Review beautiful charts in Data Studio. Pin to dashboards or let the system learn.

Full flow (visual)
flowchart LR U[User] Shell[Inspector UI] API[POST inspector chat] Sem[Semantic context] Mem[Memory injection] Agent[Agent loop] Tools[Tools and Databricks] Studio[Data Studio] Learn[Bandits and Marcus] U --> Shell Shell --> API API --> Sem API --> Mem Sem --> Agent Mem --> Agent Agent --> Tools Tools --> Studio Studio --> Shell API --> Learn
Go deeper (click to expand)
Agent Loop Internals src/lib/inspector/agent-loop.ts
The core reasoning engine. Uses Bedrock ConverseStream.
Loop: while loops < max → send prompt → stream deltas (text / thinking / toolUse) → run tools in parallel → append results → repeat.
Collects a full Trajectory of every tool call (SQL excerpt, timing, success/failure).
Supports prompt caching and Anthropic extended thinking.
Tools & Execution
Primary tool = databricks_sql. Others include semantic lookups and memory recall.
Tools are declared to the model. When the model calls one, we execute it and feed the string result back as a tool message.
All tool activity is recorded in the trajectory for learning and debugging.
Results, Studio & Governance
Results go through profiler → recommender → compiler (DSL → ECharts).
Stored in studio_query_results + studio_insights.
While looking at results you can promote definitions, resolve ambiguous entities, or pin the whole thing to a dashboard.
What Inspector teaches the system
After every turn:
• Memory records what was injected and how useful it was (attribution)
• Bandits get observations for model/tool scoring
• Marcus creates reflections (first-turn and full trajectory)
This is how the system gets smarter over time.
Common pitfalls & edge cases
• Context mode is per-session — easy to forget you switched to “Warehouse Only”.
• If no good semantic models or embeddings exist, answers become vague.
• Tool errors in the middle don’t stop the whole run — you may see partial results.
• 300 second Vercel timeout is a hard limit on long agent runs.
Quick examples
User message:
"Top 5 products by revenue last quarter"
One Trajectory entry:
{ tool: "databricks_sql", durationMs: 1840, status: "success" }

Metrics /agent-lab/metrics

Purpose: Faceted, searchable catalog of governed metrics and definitions. The single source of truth for what "revenue", "churn", etc. mean.

Two lenses: Govern (authoring, promotion) and Explore (search + usage in Inspector).
Backed by semantic_* tables. Promotion gate applies. Directly controls what Inspector can resolve and recommend.
Teach /agent-lab/teach + /digest

Purpose: Deliberate knowledge extraction mode (different from normal Inspector). Uses Marcus reflection to produce high-quality candidates for FOER memory (not direct injection).

Flow:
1
Reflective chat in teach modality.
2
Live LearningRail extracts candidates.
3
Conflict resolution + Digest review.
4
Synthesis DAG → FOER promotion.
Performance Lab /performance-lab
Purpose: Evaluation surface for boost configs, model variants, and agent behaviors.
Run controlled comparisons. Results feed directly into bandit scoring and Marcus reflections.
Key: BoostTabs component, comparison runs, lift metrics.
Bandits /agent-lab/bandits

Purpose: Learn which models, tools, and boost configs win per task — from real Inspector runs and Performance Lab experiments (CTSGV scoring).

• Write path: scoreRun → reportToBandit → writeBanditObservation
• UI: Born chart, task heatmap, posterior timeline, live feed
• Read API: /api/backfill/agent-lab/bandits
• Feeds: Marcus reflections, model dispatch, cost/quality tradeoffs
Memory — group overview

FOER (Field-Operational Experience Recall) = org operating memory: rules in platform_agent_memory, injected in phases at chat time, grown overnight from traces — no model fine-tuning.

• Daytime: retrieve → inject → run → recordInjection → attribute outcomes
• Overnight: synthesize sweep → curate → refine → cluster/reclassify (DAG)
• Surfaces: FOER story UI, Ops, Contributions, Teach, Home memory card
• Flags: MEMORY_INJECT_ENABLED, phase budgets, reputation gate

Semantic Layer Foundation

Purpose: Governed business dictionary (entities, dimensions, measures) in Aurora so Inspector, dashboards, and metrics always resolve “revenue” to the same SQL.

• 12-step playbook: harvest → author → promote → consume
• Draft → candidate → governed lifecycle + promotion gate
• SQL compiler + context-builder for agent prompts
• Estate jobs T0–T4 bootstrap semantic models

Tables: platform_semantic_*, entity mappings, NL intent. Feeds Inspector disambiguation and dashboard widgets.

Data Studio

Purpose: One visualization engine for the whole product — profile tabular results, recommend chart types, compile Chart DSL → ECharts, persist for replay and dashboard pins.

Profiler — shape, cardinality, distributions (lib/studio/profiler.ts)
Recommender — chart type + confidence (recommender.ts)
Compiler — DSL + themes (compiler.ts, DataStudio.tsx)

APIs: /api/studio/results, /api/agent-lab/studio/insights. Storage: studio_query_results, studio_insights.

Auth & RBAC

Purpose: Identity (NextAuth: Azure AD + credentials) and authorization on every page and API — roles, policies, ownership, audit.

• middleware.ts — route protection
• resolveAuth — session + bearer for APIs
• lib/rbac.ts — owner-or-permission
• Govern Users / Policies UI + writeAudit

Live role refresh each request. Gates Inspector, promotion, harvest jobs, dashboard share.

Marcus & Workbench

Purpose: Post-turn reflection — turn Inspector/Teach trajectories into structured lessons for FOER memory and bandit scoring (non-blocking, async).

• evaluateInspectorFirstTurn — intent & quick wins
• evaluateTrajectoryReflection — tools/SQL path
• Outputs: memory candidates, bandit observations
• Stored on session for History replay

Pairs with Self-Improving Memory synthesis DAG (reflect → label → curate…).

Self-Improving Memory

Estate Overview

Purpose: At-a-glance health of the entire harvested data estate.

Shows coverage %, staleness, queued jobs, last successful harvest per source. Entry point to Catalog, Entities, Jobs, etc.
Catalog

Purpose: Discovery and browsing of all scanned objects in the warehouse.

Two main tabs (e.g. All Objects / Recent Changes). Deep links to Object Detail. Search + filters powered by harvested metadata and embeddings.
Directly feeds harvested context mode in Inspector.
Entities

Purpose: Business concept definitions mapped to physical tables/views.

Core of the Semantic Layer. Author mappings here (or via Mapper tool). Used by context-builder to ground Inspector questions.
See also platform_entity_mapping and semantic promotion flow.
Lineage
Purpose: Visual data + semantic lineage.
Shows upstream/downstream table dependencies and how semantic entities relate to physical objects. Critical for trust and impact analysis when changing sources.
Mapper
Purpose: Authoring tool for entity-to-physical mappings.
UI for creating and managing platform_entity_mapping records. Supports multiple physical realizations per business entity.
Silo Finder
Purpose: Detect data silos and orphaned objects.
Scans for tables that are not mapped to any entity, have no recent activity, or are disconnected from the main graph. Helps keep the estate healthy and governed.
Object Detail

Purpose: Deep canonical view of a single harvested object.

Shows: T0-T3 artifacts, column profiles, embeddings, entity mappings, PII flags, enrichment results. Actions: re-harvest, resolve PII, trigger enrich, view lineage.
Users

Purpose: User provisioning, role assignment, and live access control.

Admin UI for assigning roles. Uses access/* APIs. Roles and permissions are live-refreshed on every request via middleware and resolveAuth.
See also rbac.ts and the owner-or-permission pattern used across APIs.
Policies
Purpose: Fine-grained policy management.
CRUD on policy_entry. Special PATCH /api/policies/[id] endpoint for targeted updates. Policies feed into permission checks alongside roles.
Audit Log
Purpose: Immutable, system-wide audit trail.
Every significant action (logins, promotions, harvests, policy changes, etc.) writes via the writeAudit helper. Used for compliance and debugging.
Docs (Catalog)
Purpose: Versioned documentation for Agents and Tools.
The same catalog data used at runtime inside Inspector (attached agents/tools). Supports full review, versioning, and forking workflow.
Powers the "catalog APIs" used by the agent loop.
